Source: University of Georgia Cooperative Extension (fieldreport.caes.uga.edu, Winterize outdoor pipes now, before they freeze, and related pieces), seen October 30 2026 only as search-result text, the pages themselves could not be opened in this run. Facts used: freezing can burst exposed pipes; hoses can be disconnected from faucets; exposed valves and pipes can be wrapped. Also opened in full: the EPA WaterSense Fix a Leak Week page, which says check an in-ground irrigation system each spring for frost damage, not used on the card. No cost, no instruction beyond what UGA says, each row names a professional.
headline:
Before The First Freeze
A Look At Outdoor Faucets
titan_line: Echo, the University of Georgia (UGA) Cooperative Extension has a few simple notes on outdoor pipes and hoses before freezing weather.
rows: UGA Extension says a frozen exposed pipe can burst. A licensed plumber can look at yours.
UGA Extension says hoses can be disconnected from the faucet. A plumber can say more about yours.
Exposed valves and pipes can be wrapped, per UGA Extension. Ask a professional about the ones at your home.
echo_line: My hose is still on the spigot? …Oh. I'd go look at it this weekend.
source: University of Georgia Cooperative Extension, winterizing outdoor pipes · seen October 30, 2026
disclaimer: General home information, not an inspection or advice about any home. Ask a licensed plumber about yours.
